title: Blessing the Name and the Crown of Mercy
english: Your ages will not end, for your generations are from age to age (Ps 102:1b). But one should not take the ages of the wills chronologically, for time is not spoken of in this way. Nor does His being end, since His nature remains incorruptible, being alone possessing immortality.

One must not take 'sons of God' entirely according to the flesh, but according to instruction and the imitation of a way of life. For in this way some were called sons of the prophets, because they had perhaps become like them according to the prophetic manner. And Paul, a slave of Christ, has sons: Silvanus and Timothy and those near to them. And it happened that those benefiting from these were their seed. The children previously mentioned will dwell with Paul in the heavenly tabernacles, as will those being directed with them and their seed forever.

Others say that the composite man often speaks of himself as if he were others, saying, 'My soul' or 'My body.' And Paul, indeed, uses this practice, sometimes saying, 'I call God to witness upon my soul,' and sometimes implying, 'My body.' They say this by taking [the parts] as we say a people, rulers, and overseers of a city are not always different from the city itself (for it is filled from among them), but are a different rank of the whole city (for the rulers alone are not the city, nor the councilors privately, nor the people by themselves), but together they are the city—not so, even if the composite man is not another from the soul and the body (for from these two he is composed), but the soul of the whole is called as another of it.

Thus, the one who exhorts his own soul to bless the Lord is not 'uncomposite.' And those saying the soul is the spirit do not say it is such, but that it is under it, having its care. Within it, he calls upon every rational power of man. For it is not to be heard of the Savior saying, 'The kingdom of heaven is within you' (Luke 17:21). And do not view the 'internal' things as something else; for the powers we have, which are resting, are said to be able to act well within us. It is necessary to stir these up and turn them toward activity.

Through which we bless the name of the Lord. For the holy name blesses not powers, but good activities. Even the Savior says to those partaking of virtue and divine knowledge: 'The kingdom of God is within you' (Luke 17:21), saying only once: 'Seek the foundations of faith and virtue within yourselves, being rational and having become according to the image of God; seek not the good outside yourselves.'

Sins are diseases of the soul. For he says, 'My soul, what harm hast thou done to thee?' (Ps 102:3b). He redeems life from corruption, so that you may no longer live a life according to corruption and passion, but in incorruption, loving the Lord Jesus. And providing you an incorruptible body in the resurrection, he redeems your life from corruption.

And he crowns you also in mercy and compassion, the material of this crown being almsgiving and compassion. Just as others receive the crown of righteousness and the incorruptible crown of glory, woven from righteousness and upright glory, so also you, through mercy and compassion which you have worked, shall be crowned, according to 'Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy' (Matt 5:7).

And not thus is the better: not so much that I shall be emboldened in the struggling, but because you are being merciful and pitied by the Lord, you shall be crowned, the Lord returning to your intellect the crown of graces. For by the grace of God and not of our own works we are saved, and we do not deserve sufferings in this present time for the sake of the glory to be revealed to us; so also he crowns us, not looking toward our own striving, but toward his own mercy and compassion.

And fill your desire also with good things. For he gives good things to those asking him. Since even the desiring of good things happens to be asking for them, giving to you all things, he fills your desire with good things through longing; for every desire of the righteous is good.

And since you are becoming according to the image and likeness of God and have become fit to enter into the essence in advance of the good, but having flown away from heedlessness, you cast away virtue both practical and intellectual; without which, being suspended, you would rise to the height, know that you have the power to grow wings, if you should wish it.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: From Shadows to Spiritual Reality
english: Working through God. And this shall be to you, your youth being renewed according to the eagle. For just as this old feather is cast off, and immediately it grows new wings, so also you, having grown old through wickedness, are renewed from your antiquity, and your youth comes in completion, and those who once used strong wings are not so, but now being clothed with new ones, you may be lifted up into heaven toward all those who have waited for God. For those waiting for the Lord shall change strength, they shall become wing-bearing like eagles, they shall run and shall run the course.

Father of mercies and alone good is the Lord, who performs acts of mercy, showing compassion to all, doing good (Ps 102:6). God also, toward those being wronged by the devil and by wickedness, making judgment, sent his only Son to heal and to set free those being oppressed by Satan, redeeming souls from bondage and from injustice, having torn the handwriting of our debt and having nailed it to the cross. The one holding us, the devil, had made us debtors, through whom we were practicing, having set up the handwriting of our debt for him. We were rescued from all our injustice, God making judgment for those being wronged, so that through the blood of his Son Jesus Christ we might be cleansed from all injustice, not only the injustice by which we were being wronged but also the injustice which we were practicing. From here we learn, according to the exhortation of Paul, the difference between being wronged and doing wrong. For to those being wronged God performs judgment, doing them good, but to those doing wrong he brings punishment, so that they do not inherit the divine promise: For those who do wrong shall not inherit the kingdom of God (Ps 102:7/1 Cor 6:9).

Virtues are called parallel. For he who says, 'Lord, make known to me your ways' (Ps 102:7), it is worthy that virtues become manifest to him; and that part by Paul toward Elymas, saying, 'You will not cease turning away the straight ways of the Lord' (Acts 13:10), presents the same, signifying that virtues are also the wills of God. And otherwise the coming thing might be understood; for since God gave the law of the things to come through Moses, having a shadow of them, but not every part...

This law bears an image and a type of the intelligible and spiritual, as if it were to move from the sensible things to the spiritual and original ones by a way of analogy. And the Lord will teach such transitions—fittingly, concerning these transitions it is said, 'He made known His ways to Moses' (Ps 105:5). For who else besides Moses, having learned from God how to ascend from the sensible circumcision and bodily sacrifice and the other shadowy things to the truth, knew this way? For He made known His ways to him.

But also, if anyone is a son of Israel, if it is not said, 'Israel is my chosen one,' how will he understand the wills of God, which are made known to the discerning ones by Him, such as the Jews who, hurrying in secret, circumcise not the flesh but the heart; and they also offer a sacrifice of righteousness and pleasingness to God, not as a spiritual sacrifice. All these things spoken are the Lord, since God is true; but a true God is not in the excellence of the aforementioned virtues, but is the source and essence of them. Therefore, we also take courage that He will not be angry with us for having sinned, in order to complete and destroy this. For this was 'He will be angry unto the end,' that is, to remain in anger as an end, and the anger toward the gods is destruction. He does not become angry unto the end, nor does He remain for an age. For the deceiver does not have lasting anger: 'When the anger of my spirit is kindled, I shall be healed' (Ps 102:13).

But the mercy of God takes its beginning upon the earth, according to what was said: 'The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord' (Ps 32:5). If mercy, beginning from there, becomes directed toward the pious, it lifts them up and suspends them upon the height of the heavens: 'For great is your mercy, O Lord, unto the heavens' (Ps 36:5). For ascending into the kingdom of heaven happens more by the mercy of God than by anything else. And the saving virtues appear to be sunrises, while sins are sunsets, entirely deprived of light. Since no one can exist in both virtue and wickedness, he who has associated himself with the aforementioned sunrises, as if to dwell in them, [is like] the one in Eden, planted by God according to sunrises.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Endurance of Mercy and the Nature of Commandments
english: Having been distanced from paradise, the previously spoken evils of the interpreted Easts hold such a distance from himself. For the evils are far from the virtues.

But as one in the Easts has the previously spoken evils distanced from him by God, so he who is in them, desiring to sin by himself and not from God, is not distanced from the Easts, but is cast out of paradise. But even after these things have happened through disobedience to the divine commands, Jesus comes upon the evils according to 'Make way for him who is stepping upon the evils, the Lord is the law to him' (Ps 102:13), and he will not stay there long, but coming to the pain, saying 'With me you shall be in paradise.' For providing a remission of sins, he removes the evils from the rising toward paradise.

Rather, God excessively and super-abundantly pities those who fear him (Ps 102:13), having set them into the rank of his sons, making known to each of us the creature. For he did not create anything hating, but knowing the hearts of men, he fashioned them individually as he saw fit for each of us. And we have power and a starting point, and these he gives upon us having them by energy to become his sons. It is possible to grasp that he himself knows our creature and thus: let him take experience of our creature; having become flesh, he assumed a natural disposition so as to consider us sons of himself.

Not as a creator of our nature did he create the weakness. For even if not all our construction is from dust (for we have a spiritual nature in ourselves, becoming an icon and likeness of God), but rather in supplications toward God, deeming him a gatherer and benefactor, we say that he brings forward the lesser and weaker of those in us: 'Remember, Lord, what dust we are; therefore help our weakness and our poverty' (Ps 102:14). Following 'Remember, Lord, what dust we are,' it forbids not the inner man, but the outer things lying ahead. For according to the present and after the flesh, we have certain days that complete the extending time of the life after the flesh, surpassing it like a parching meadow.

He sings along with the others, and Isaiah says: 'All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is like the flower of the grass; the sun rises and withers the grass, and its flower falls' (Isa 40:6-8). These things represent the glories, honors, and all the prosperities existing in this life which seem to those living in the flesh to be abundant, yet they depart like a flower and grass, and wither as if they had never even existed (Ps 102:17-18).

You should also perceive in another way the children of righteous men as zealots for their works. Thus, the mercy of God toward those who fear Him is indescribably extended from age to age (Ps 102:17-18). For He does not sometimes show mercy and sometimes not; for being good by nature, He always shows mercy. Moreover, righteousness is the spouse of this mercy; it is not limited by time, but extends to all generations, remaining upon the sons of sons and through all succession, so that He may always have this righteousness with those who guard the covenant of God from age to age, who are also inscribed as heirs of the coming promises through their doing of good. For those guarding it will also remember the commandments of God by doing them. For these are given not as a mere memory, but a memory for the purpose of doing. And regarding that which they are given for the purpose of doing, the Savior also establishes, saying: 'He who has my commandments and does them, he is the one who loves me' (John 14:15). For the promises are the reward and inheritance not of their memory alone, but of their doing.

And in other places it has been said that God is not in a place, but it is said that He dwells in heaven through a certain following and economy. Accordingly, it has been said that they have prepared for Him even here in heaven, that is, they have established the throne of His kingdom and His rule, not only of those in heaven, but of all, holding and dominating universally (Ps 102:19). One should not regard the prophet as a man, but rather the Holy Spirit within him, commanding the angels regarding the things at hand; for all His angels (meaning the Lord's) say, 'Bless Him' (Ps 103:20). The Spirit commands all the angels, being their essence. If this is so, how did some dare with audacity...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
